For h∈K, substitute k↦hk in the weak scalar integral using left invariance to obtain σ(h)A(T)=A(T)π(h); hence every image is an intertwiner. If T intertwines, its integrand equals T for all k, so A(T)=T. Therefore A²=A and the range is Hom_K. If Hom_K contains a nonzero S, then A(S)=S and ||A||≥1 after normalizing S; otherwise A is the zero map. This proves the precise norm statement. AC is used for normalized Haar and Hilbert Riesz; no norm-continuity claim for arbitrary T.
